title: Samsung S10 & Android 10
body:
Hi

Yesterday I updated my Samsung S10 to Android 10

Unfortunately, Xdrip does not work anymore
I use Dexcom G6
I have the latest version of 5.12.2019 on the run and also the app settings for system settings is turned on unfortunately it does not work. Does anyone have a tip or idea?

Thanks and regards

Dragan

I have the same problem with my S10 & G6 since the Android 10 update. I have tried through all xdrip settings combinations and guides and fixes, without success (and lost my last 6m of xdrip data, luckily it is uploaded to Nightscout). Reading the logs, it seems to have to do with BLE. xdrip was able to read the sensor only once every time I forgot it and restarted the collector, but not again thereafter. Funnily enough, the Dexcom app has no problems.

I have now been successfully using the following workaround, similar to what the person above me says: The official Dexcom app reads the G6 with Share enabled. On my Nightscout Heroku app, I have set up Dexcom Share as the source for BG readings. Then, in the xdrip app, I have set up Dexcom Share as a BG source, while also syncing my treatments to Nightscout. So in the end, I have the same functionality as before (e.g. using xdrip to manage my diabetes and having everything uploaded to Nightscout), with the drawback that xdrip sometimes misses the readings from Share for a few minutes (but its usually at max. 1 reading behind) and it is dependent on internet connection. But even without internet, the Dexcom app is running in the background and can be used.

Let us hope that either a new Samsung or xdrip update fixes this soon. If anyone has success, please share your strategy.

Hello Jesaca7,

I'm sorry that you too are having problems with xDrip with the Dexcom G5
system on your Samsung S10 using Android 10.

Unfortunately, my Samsung S10 has stopped working again so I don't have any
advice that would help you.

Here's what I can tell you.

I installed xDrip on my Samsung S10 when it was using Android 9. Everything
was working great for a month until I upgraded to Android 10.

After the upgrade, xDrip only worked for a day or so. I called Dexcom
support thinking that it was a problem with the G5 transmitter.

Dexcom replaced my transmitter and sensor. xDrip and my Samsung S10 worked
for 4 days before stopping again.

I researched the posts on NightScout's website and tried the suggestions I
found. I tried different xDrip versions going back to April 2019. I tried
flashing my phone back to Android Pie 9. Flashing did not work because I'm
using a Verizon locked phone. I had to do a factory reset which wiped my
phone of all my programs, data, photos, music, basically everything.

Even though I had backed everything up, it still took me a week to get
everything back the way it was before the reset.

I reinstalled xDrip. No success even while trying several different
versions.

After reading a post about someone having success with Android 10 using the
latest xDrip version, I upgraded back to Android 10. I installed the latest
version of xDrip.

Success!

But for only 4 days.

I called Dexcom Support  who determined that my sensor was bad because both
my Dexcom Receiver and phone were getting the same faulty inconsistent
readings.

I installed a new sensor last night but have not started using xDrip again,
just my Dexcom Receiver.

To summarize:

- All of these issues started with the Android 10 upgrade.

- Trying different versions did not resolve the problem.

- Going back to Android 9 with a factory reset did not resolve the problem.

- Trying different versions again did not resolve the problem.

@dhansen7 I did not remove cache or data last time. I actually restored from backup this last time. But I had solid readings for  a LONG time yesterday, then at night after disconnecting from my watch things went south.

Found another workaround;

"Forget Bluetooth device in xdrip.
Go to Settings - Apps - See all Apps - (3 dots on top right corner) - Show system apps - Bluetooth - Delete Data

Then you can try to connect with your miao miao again."

Taken from this thread:

https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/issues/1001

Seems to have successfully got my miaomiao to show as connected in xdrip

This is also on the latest nightly build (26th Jan 2020) - followed above workaround and it connected successfully, recieved data and is working. 

Will report back tomorrow about how long-term this fix is.

I've received some logs from a S10+ user which show that samsung are blocking the xDrip wake up timing. This is the sort of thing we've seen from them before with non-standard power saving features.  For anyone having problems I would look again if you can find any other hidden power saving whitelist for apps etc.

Due to that, as this is also known from OnePlus: Samsung 10+ could test if it helps to lock xdrip in the recent apps list (open recent apps, scroll to xdrip picture, then there should be a open lock, or a possible menu, where the app could be locked). I have seen that this lock was checked by the additional poversaving routines of some phone firmwares. Maybe this helps...

UPDATE: This has worked for me. I've also changed power settings in my S10 to stop battery optimisation. I've turned off the "Adaptive Battery" settings in android settings, and also turned off "Put unused apps to sleep".
I reset my s10 with Android 10 to factory settings today.  xdrip and AndroidAPS installed in current versions.  since then both apps work great.  I'm so happy
